english: Let $A(3,1,0)$, $B(1,3,2)$ and $C(-1,1,4)$ be three points. Let $L$ denote the set of all points $P$ in space such that $PA=PB=PC$. Then the point at which $L$ meets the plane $x+y+z=5$ is
hindi: माना $A(3,1,0)$, $B(1,3,2)$ तथा $C(-1,1,4)$ तीन बिन्दु हैं। माना $L$ त्रिविम समष्टि के उन सभी बिन्दुओं $P$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए $PA=PB=PC$ है। तब वह बिन्दु, जिस पर $L$ समतल $x+y+z=5$ से मिलता है, है
solution: So $L$ is the line $\dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{y}{0}=\dfrac{z-1}{1}$ (the intersection of two perpendicular-bisector planes; it is perpendicular to plane $ABC$ through its circumcentre)
solution_full: Let $P(x,y,z)$ be a point of $L$. The condition $PA=PB=PC$ is equivalent to the two equations $PA^2=PB^2$ and $PA^2=PC^2$.
So $PA^2=PB^2$ gives the plane $x-y-z+1=0$, the perpendicular-bisector plane of $AB$.
So $PA^2=PC^2$ gives the plane $x-z+1=0$, the perpendicular-bisector plane of $AC$.
The two planes are not parallel (normals $(1,-1,-1)$ and $(1,0,-1)$), so $L$ is their line of intersection. From $z=x+1$ and $x-y-z+1=0$ we get $y=0$.

Hence $L:\ \dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{y}{0}=\dfrac{z-1}{1}$, that is, the points $(t,0,t+1)$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$. Its direction $(1,0,1)$ is parallel to $\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}$, so $L$ is the normal to the plane $ABC$ through the circumcentre of the triangle.
Substituting $(t,0,t+1)$ in $x+y+z=5$: $2t+1=5\Rightarrow t=2$, giving the point $(2,0,3)$.
The other options fail: $(1,0,2)$ is the circumcentre of triangle $ABC$ but not on the plane, $(3,0,2)$ and $(2,1,2)$ lie on the plane but are not equidistant from $A$, $B$, $C$.
originality_note: New: the line is never given; it is defined as the locus of points equidistant from three points (two perpendicular-bisector planes, way 3) and then cut by a plane. Closest known: the textbook exercise of a point on a coordinate plane equidistant from three points. Different because: the locus is a full line that must be identified first, and the plane x+y+z=5 is not a coordinate plane.

concept_use.Equation of a line: L is obtained as the line of intersection of the planes x-y-z+1=0 and x-z+1=0 and written in symmetric form x/1 = y/0 = (z-1)/1 before meeting the plane.

stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line and plane is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy and numpy, is unique and equals the Answer Plan; the options have one form and exactly one is correct. Checked that the three points are not collinear, so the locus is a line. Changed: No change.
key_step: Recognising that PA=PB=PC is a line (two perpendicular-bisector planes) and writing it in symmetric form.
justification: Routine chain: two plane equations, their line of intersection, then a point on a plane. No insight beyond seeing the locus as a line. Same demand as the routine vector-geometry chain of 2026-P2-Q1 (L2), above the one-step 2023-P2-Q4 (L1).
